editorial.headline: Insurance Loss Assessment: Open Nationally, Clear in Bali
editorial.standfirst: For insurance claim assessment and consulting on insured objects, this activity is open to foreign investment nationally and is not blocked by Bali’s PMA moratorium.
editorial.body:
Insurance claims call for a disciplined assessment of what has been claimed and, where needed, advice concerning the object insured. This activity is the business of assessing insurance claims and providing consulting services on insured objects. In the loss-adjuster role, the work is performed when a claim occurs. The scope is therefore precise: it centres on the claim assessment itself and/or consultation about the insured object. A company registering here is describing a practice built around those two stated functions, with loss adjustment attached to the moment of claim.

The registration is stated to be open at every scale named in the record—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar. That makes scale an availability point, not a rewriting of the underlying activity: whether the business is registered as Mikro or Besar, the described work remains claim assessment and/or consulting on insured objects. The scope adds an important timing note for loss adjustment: it is undertaken when a claim has occurred. For founders, that keeps the reading grounded in the record, with the enterprise focused on assessment and consulting in the insurance-object context.

At the national level, this is a TERBUKA activity for foreign investment, and its maximum foreign ownership is 100%. In practical ownership terms, the record does not impose a national foreign-share ceiling below full ownership. Its PMA source is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. A foreign founder can therefore take the national position at face value: the activity is open to PMA, with the stated 100% maximum, and it is available across the four listed scales. That national reading is necessary, but it is not the entire local answer for a Bali-based registration.

The local answer is favourable as well: a foreign founder can register this activity in Bali today, because it is not blocked for PMA registration by the provincial moratorium. Bali marks the activity OK_or_HIGHER_RISK and gives the operative reason: at the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. Bali’s permanent, island-wide rule blocks PMA for Low and Medium-Low risk activities; this activity is expressly recorded as outside that block. The honest conclusion is simple and exact: nationally the foreign-ownership maximum is 100%, and in Bali the moratorium does not bar PMA registration for this activity.
